expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "CI never ran old code + new schema — and that's the state that exists for real during every deploy, while old pods drain. Those three call sites throw column does not exist."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "Two PRs: Now: the three code changes only... Later (next week): the DROP, alone, after you've confirmed from query logs."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "The data is gone at that instant... point-in-time restore of the whole database to before the migration — not a revert."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Normally Friday is fine — you revert in ten minutes. But once the column is dropped, revert makes it worse... Recovery is a database restore, with a weekend on-call rotation."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "Recovery is a database restore, with a weekend on-call rotation."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "a CI check that fails when a migration containing DROP/destructive ALTER lands in the same PR as application code."

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "ship the code half this afternoon with confidence. Hold the DROP for Monday-to-Wednesday."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "the three code changes only... Fully reversible — revert is a normal deploy" vs the DROP.
